_doc: ⚑ S283 (2026-11-01) — PERIOD REFERENCES for the four era websites (tools/gen_era_sites.mjs → public/sites/). The same rule as links.json and the same refusal: every `url` below must appear VERBATIM in the document named in its `verifiedIn`, or the generator and `npm test` fail. Every row here is one that docs/reinterp/REFERENCE_LINKS_CHECKED_2026-10-31.md marks 'Works. HTTP 200' (the pages marked BLOCKED, FAIL, dead or [VERIFY SOURCE] are left out). They are archived pages and contemporary articles to LOOK AT — the sites show no picture from them and make no request to them; a visitor who follows a link opens it in a new tab. `n` is the row number in that document. Nothing here is a claim of the piece: these are where the period looked like this.

1997.label: NARTH home page, December 1997 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A clinical-looking page. Grey background, a coin logo, a long list, two “NEW” starbursts.

1997.label: Love in Action home page, December 1998 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A cream page with one big link: “Click here to continue”. The page is marked 1997.

1997.label: PFOX home page, November 1998 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A plain white page with a green hit counter at the bottom left.

1997.label: Exodus home page, April 1999 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A light yellow page, two rainbow-coloured rules and a plain bullet list.

1997.label: New Direction (Canada) home page, January 2000 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A white page with green bold text and a row of text links at the foot.

1997.label: Christianity Today, September 1998 — a report on the newspaper ad campaign
1997.note: A contemporary report. The site shows a cookie banner first.

1997.label: Dignity USA, 1998 — gay Catholics answer the ex-gay ads
1997.note: A short response from a Catholic LGBT group, on a plain page.

1997.label: “Truth in Love”, the sponsor’s page for its two television spots (capture of December 2001)
1997.note: The spots are from 1999, offered with a script, a download and a call line. No number is written here.

1997.label: “Truth in Love”, the script of the spot “Mom” (capture of November 2001)
1997.note: A two-column table, On Screen and Audio. It describes the spot shot by shot and ends on a black card.

1997.label: “Truth in Love”, the script of the spot “Families” (capture of November 2001)
1997.note: The second spot, in the same table format. It names no programme.

1997.label: “Truth in Love”, the newspaper ads of 1998 (capture of November 2001)
1997.note: Four newspaper ads, with the sponsor’s list of 19 supporting organisations.

1997.label: OUTPOST Inc., an Exodus International branch in Minnesota, January 1998 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A home page still being set up, whose first offer is a commercial to download: “HOPE for CHANGE”.

1997.label: OUTPOST Inc., the “HOPE for CHANGE” commercial as a QuickTime file, 1998 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A television-style ad offered on a website. The file opens in a new tab; this site does not play it.

1997.label: OUTPOST Inc., its links page, January 1998 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: Other ministry branches in the state, and an email address for “hope”.

1997.label: Bridges Across, its mailing list, December 1998 (Internet Archive capture)
1997.note: A dialogue list between ex-gay and gay Christians, up to forty messages a day: what a 1990s list felt like.

2003.label: Exodus home page, July 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: Two large smiling portraits, a round logo and an orange image-button menu.

2003.label: Exodus North America home page, February 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A crimson swoosh, a “Top News” box and a footer of image buttons.

2003.label: Love in Action home page, July 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A blue banner and a strip of fourteen smiling faces across the page.

2003.label: NARTH home page, July 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: Centred text, red underlined headline links and a small left menu.

2003.label: PFOX home page, July 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A “Best Viewed With Internet Explorer” line and a tell-a-friend form.

2003.label: Regeneration home page, June 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A waterfall photograph and four menu words drawn as images.

2003.label: Exodus North America, “Regeneration Books” catalogue, June 2001 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A book catalogue with a dark blue left menu of sixteen categories.

2003.label: An ex-gay links directory, “as of 4-23-2003” (GeoCities page, captured 2008)
2003.note: A huge hand-made link list with a colour legend and web rings.

2003.label: “Truth in Love” campaign page, December 2001 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: The sponsor's own page for its 1999 television spots. Two video stills and a call line.

2003.label: “Truth in Love”, the script of one spot, November 2001 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A two-column table, On Screen and Audio, with the end card on black.

2003.label: Christianity Today, September 1999 — a report on television stations refusing the ads
2003.note: A contemporary report. The site shows a cookie banner first.

2003.label: International Healing Foundation home page, July 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A teal page with family photos and a rainbow-banded list that begins “WE BELIEVE THAT”: the movement's credo set in the rainbow's own colours.

2003.label: International Healing Foundation home page, October 2002, with its page-view counter (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: The same site a year earlier, counting its visitors since March 2001.

2003.label: International Healing Foundation, its “Institute” page, October 2002 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: Training to “help” homosexuality change, offered as a therapy institute.

2003.label: “The Map”, a twenty-lesson change curriculum on CD, its Journey page, 2007 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A conversion programme sold as an interactive CD, with printable journals and an audio introduction.

2003.label: A worship song page, “A Father's Love”, on becomingreal.org, April 2004 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A song of the prodigal son set beside a painting, with an mp3 to download: worship used as the ministry's invitation.

2003.label: “Interview With Jesus”, a Flash “movie” site, June 2004 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A slideshow film sold on DVD and shared by link: the visual grammar of the period's Christian web.

2003.label: Bridges Across, its web forums, December 2003 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: The same community five years later, on registered-only web forums with a confidentiality page: what a 2003 forum looked like.

2003.label: “Christians in Recovery” workbook software, Self-HelpSoftware.com, 2008 (Internet Archive capture)
2003.note: A faith-based 12-step workbook sold as desktop software for Windows, Mac and Palm — the shape of the piece’s own software.

2016.label: “For girls”, becomingreal.org, April 2004 (Internet Archive capture)
2016.note: A question page for teenage girls: “I think I might be…”, each answered by the ministry. The lineage of the women's material Vera edits.

2016.label: “The Map”, its Stories page: video testimonies as proof, 2007 (Internet Archive capture)
2016.note: Testimonies offered as downloads, as hope and “deliverance”: the testimony economy before the platforms.

2026.label: GLAAD, “Build for Everyone” (2026 AI report): the case study on AI and conversion “therapy”
2026.note: In April 2025 a major AI model, built to give “both sides”, suggested conversion therapy to someone asking about “unwanted same-sex attraction”. The documented ground under Second Thoughts.
